title: I Reverse Engineered the Bloomberg Terminal and Made It FREE
description:
Get the free prompt: https://lewiswjackson.com/q/bbterm-desc-l1
Learn how to quant trade with AI (+ $500 trading competition): https://lewiswjackson.com/q/bbterm-desc-l2

A Bloomberg Terminal costs $31,980 a year for one seat, on a two-year contract. I reverse engineered it from Bloomberg's public pages and public data, and called mine Amber Terminal. You paste one prompt into Claude Code or Codex and it installs on your own computer in about 30 seconds: 45 function codes like WEI, DES, GP, WIRP, OMON and ECO, four panels, the Bloomberg-style keyboard, news, SEC filings, rates, options and a backtester with quant checks. Mac, Windows or Linux.

Claude connects to it, so you can ask about the markets in plain English and it answers from the same screens. The prompt page has 12 playbooks for trading with it: a morning brief, whether the earnings move is already priced, what the Fed is priced to do, insiders buying their own stock, and red flags in company filings.

Every number comes from a public source with no account or API key, and the DATA screen shows where each one comes from. Some stock and futures prices run up to 15 minutes behind. It doesn't have Bloomberg's newsroom or its chat.

Chapters
0:00 A $32,000 Bloomberg Terminal, rebuilt
1:09 What a Bloomberg Terminal is
2:06 Charts, news and every market
2:36 Ask Claude about any of it
3:32 How to use it for trading with Claude
4:53 Edge or luck? Backtest with quant checks
5:44 Install it with one prompt
5:54 Stuck? Where to get help
6:14 What should I reverse engineer next?

Educational content, not financial advice. Trading involves risk, and past results, backtests included, don't predict future ones. The strategy competition uses simulated money; competition rules: https://www.part-timequant.com/competition-terms
Amber Terminal is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Bloomberg L.P. Bloomberg and Bloomberg Terminal are trademarks of Bloomberg Finance L.P. Charts use TradingView Lightweig
